questions.q: Let $[x]$ denote the greatest integer $\leq x$. If $f(x)=[x] and g(x)=|x|$, then the value of $f \left(g \left(\frac{8}{5}\right)\rright)-$g\lleft(f $\left(-\frac{8}{5}\right)\right)is$
questions.solution:
Given, $f(x)=[x] and g(x)=|x|$
Now,
$\begin{gathered}
f\left(\frac{-8}{5}\right)=\left[-\frac{8}{5}\right]=-2 \ldots(i)\\
g\left(\frac{8}{5}\right)=\left|\frac{8}{5}\right|=\frac{8}{5}\ldots(ii)
\end{gathered}$
Now, $f\left(g\left(\frac{8}{5}\right)\right)-g\left(f\left(-\frac{8}{5}\right)\right)=f\left(\frac{8}{5}\right)-g(-2)$
By Eqs. (i) and (ii),
$\begin{aligned}
& =\left[\frac{8}{5}\right]-|-2| \\
& =1-2 \\
& =-1
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The function $f: \boldsymbol{R} \rightarrow \boldsymbol{R}$ defined by $f(x)=\frac{x}{\sqrt{1+x^2}}$ is
questions.solution: Given that, $f(x)=\frac{x}{\sqrt{1+x^2}}$ For injective: Let $x_1, x_2 \in \boldsymbol{R}$ such that $f\left(x_1\right)=f\left(x_2\right)\Rightarrow \frac{x_1}{\sqrt{1+x_1^2}}=\frac{x_2}{\sqrt{1+x_2^2}} \Rightarrow \frac{x_1^2}{1+x_1^2}=\frac{x_2^2}{1+x_2^2}\Rightarrow x_1^2+x_1^2 x_2^2=x_2^2+x_1^2 x_2^2 \Rightarrow x_1^2=x_2^2\Rightarrow x_1=x_2$ So, $f(x)$ is injective. For surjective: Let $y=\frac{x}{\sqrt{1+x^2}}\Rightarrow y^2\left(1+x^2\right)=x^2 \Rightarrow y^2+y^2 x^2=x^2\Rightarrow x^2\left(1-y^2\right)=y^2 \Rightarrow x=\sqrt{\frac{y^2}{1-y^2}}\Rightarrow \frac{y^2}{1-y^2} \geq 0$ $\therefore y \in(-1,1)$ So, $f(x)$ is not surjective.

questions.q: Let the function $g:(-\infty, \infty) \rightarrow \left(-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right) be given by $g(u)=2 \tan ^{-1}$\left(e^u\\right)-\frac{\pi}{2}$.Then, g is
options: even and is strictly increasing in $(0, \infty)$
odd and is strictly decreasing in $(-\infty, \infty)$
odd and is strictly increasing in $(-\infty, \infty)$
neither even nor odd, but is strictly increasing in $(-\infty, \infty)$
questions.solution:
Given that $g(u)=2 \tan ^{-1}\left(e^u\right)-\frac{\pi}{2}\therefore \quad g(-u)=2 \tan ^{-1}\left(e^{-u}\right)-\frac{\pi}{2}=2 \tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{e^u}\right)-\frac{\pi}{2}=2 \cot ^{-1}\left(e^u\right)-\frac{\pi}{2}=2\left[\frac{\pi}{2}-\tan ^{-1}\left(e^u\right)\right]-\frac{\pi}{2}=\pi-2 \tan ^{-1}\left(e^u\right)-\frac{\pi}{2}=\frac{\pi}{2}-2 \tan ^{-1}\left(e^u\right)=-g(u)\therefore \quad g$ is an odd function.
Also $g^{\prime}(u)=\frac{2 e^u}{1+e^{2 u}}>0, \forall u \in(-\infty, \infty)\therefore g$ is strictly increasing on $(-\infty, \infty)$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The inverse of the function $f \left(x\right) = \log_{\mathrm{a}} \left(x + \sqrt{x^{2} + 1}\right) (where, $ a < 0, a \ne 1$) is$
questions.solution:
Let $f\left(x\right) = y$, then

$a^{y} = x + \sqrt{x^{2} + 1}$

$⇒ a^{- y} = \dfrac{1}{x + \sqrt{x^{2} + 1}}$

$⇒ a^{- y} = \dfrac{x - \sqrt{x^{2} + 1}}{- 1}$ [rationalising]

$∴ a^{y} - a^{- y} = 2x$

$⇒ x = \dfrac{1}{2} \left(a^{y} - a^{- y}\right)$

$∴ f^{- 1} \left(y\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(a^{y} - a^{- y}\right)$ & $\left[∵ f \left(x\right) =$ y ⇒ x = f^{- 1}$\left(y\right)$\right]$

$⇒ f^{- 1} $\left(x\right) =\dfrac{1}{2} \left(a^{x} - a^{- x}\right) [replacing $y$ by $x$]

Hence, option (a) is correct.

$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Let $f: R \to R$ be a function satisfying $f\left(x + y\right) = f\left(x\right) + 2y^{2} + kxy$ for all $x, y \in \mathbb{R}$. If $f  \left(1\right) = 2$ and $f\left(2\right) = 8$, then $f\left(x\right) is equal to$
questions.solution:
We have, $f\left(x + y\right) = f\left(x\right) + 2{y}^{2} + kxy$ for all $x, y \in R$

$⇒ \dfrac{f\left(x + y\right) - f\left(x\right)}{y} = 2y + kx$ for all $x \in R$

$⇒ \lim_{y \to 0}\dfrac{f\left(x + y\right) - f\left(x\right)}{y} = \lim_{y \to 0}\left(2y + kx\right)$

$⇒ {f}^{'}\left(x\right) = kx$ for all $x \in R$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{k{x}^{2}}{2} + C$ for all $x \in R$  [by integration]

But $f\left(1\right) = 2$ and $f\left(2\right) = 8$

$∴ 2 = \dfrac{k}{2} + C$ and $8 = 2k + C$

$k = 4$ and $C = 0$

Hence, $f\left(x\right) = 2{x}^{2}$ for all $x \in R$

So, option (a) is correct.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If a function $f: R \to R$ satisfy the equation $f ( x + y ) = f ( x ) + f ( y ) , ∀ x, y$ and the function $f ( x )$ is continuous at $x = 0$, then
options: $f ( x )$ is continuous for all positive real values of $x$
questions.solution:
$∵ \lim_{x \to 0}f \left(x\right) = f \left(0\right)$

Let $a$ be any point

Now, at $x = a, \lim_{x \to a}f \left(x\right) = \lim_{h \to 0}f \left(a + h\right)$

$= \lim_{h \to 0}f \left(a\right) + \lim_{h \to 0}f \left(h\right)$

$= f \left(a\right) + f \left(0\right) = f \left(a + 0\right) = f\left(a\right)$

$∴ f \left(x\right)$ is continuous at $x = a$, where $a$ is any arbitrary point.

Hence, $f \left(x\right)$ is continuous for all $x$.

questions.q: If \(f(x)=\frac{1-x}{1+x}\) the domain of \(f^{-1}(x)\) is
questions.solution:
Let \(f(x)=y\). Then \(\frac{1-x}{1+x}=y\)

Thus, \(f^{-1}(x)=\frac{1-x}{1+x}\)

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A black die and a white die are rolled. Find the probability that the number shown by the black die will be more than twice that shown by the white die.
questions.solution:
The number of favourable cases are shown below:
\$begin{array}{cl}\text{ Number on white die }$& $\text{ Number on black die }$\\ 1 & 3 \\ 1 & 4 \\ 1 & 5 \\ 1 & 6 \\ 2 & 5 \\ 2 & 6\end{array}\)
There are 6 favourable cases in which the number on black die is more than twice the number on the white die.
\begin{aligned}& \therefore $\mathrm{m}=$6 \\
& $\mathrm{n}=\text{ Total number of cases }=$6 \times6
\end{aligned}\)
( \(\therefore\) with each die there are six possibilities)
\(\therefore\) Probability \$(\mathrm{p}=\frac{\mathrm{m}}{\mathrm{n}}=\frac{6}{6 \times 6}=\frac{1}{6}$\)

questions.q: The range of the function \(f(x)=$\frac{x^2-x+1}{x^2+x+1}$\) where \($\mathrm{x} \in \mathrm{R}$\), is
questions.solution:
$$\begin{aligned}& \text{Let } y=\frac{x^2-x+1}{x^2+x+1}\\
& \Rightarrow \mathrm{x}^2(\mathrm{y}-1)+\mathrm{x}(\mathrm{y}+1)+(\mathrm{y}-1)=0 \\
& \Rightarrow x=\frac{-(y+1) \pm \sqrt{(y+1)^2-4(y-1)^2}}{2(y-1)}\\
& =\frac{-(y+1) \pm \sqrt{-3 y²+10 y-3}}{2(y-1)} \text{ is real iff }\\
& \mathrm{y}-1  ≠ 0 \Rightarrow \mathrm{y} \neq1 \\
& \text{ If } y=1 \text{ then original equation gives } \mathrm{x}=0 \text{, }\\
& \text{ so taking } \mathrm{y}=1 \\
& \text{ Also }3 y²-10 y+3 \leq 0 \\
& \Rightarrow(3 y-1)(y-3) \leq 0 \\
& \Rightarrow \mathrm{y} \in\left[\frac{1}{3},3\right] \quad \therefore \text{ Range is }\left[\frac{1}{3},3\right] \\
&
\end{aligned}$$\)

questions.q: Find the vertex of the parabola \(x²-8 y-x+19=0\).
questions.solution:
The given equation of Parabola can be written as
$\begin{aligned} \lleft(x-\frac{1}{2}\right)^2-8 y+19-\frac{1}{4}=0 \\ \text{$ and $} \lleft(x-\frac{1}{2}\right)^2=8 y-\frac{76-1}{4}\\ \text{ and } \Rightarrow\lleft(x-\frac{1}{2}\rright)^2=8\lleft(y-\frac{75}{32}\right) \therefore \text{ vertex }=\left(\frac{1}{2}, \frac{75}{32}\right)
\end{aligned}\)$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If \(y=e^{-x} \cos x\) and \(y_4+k y=0\), where \(y_4=\frac{d^4 y}{d x^4}\), then \(k=\)
questions.solution:
Let \(y=e^{-x} \cos x\)
\(\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{y}_1=-e^{-x} \sin x-e^{-x} \cos x=-e^{-x} \sin x-y \\
& y_2=-e^{-x} \cos x+e^{-x} \sin x-y_1 \\
& \Rightarrow y_2=-y-y_1+e^{-x} \sin x=-2\left(y+y_1\right) \\
& \Rightarrow y_3=-2\left(y_1+y_2\right)=-2\left(e^{-x} \sin x-y\right) \\
& \Rightarrow y_4=4 y_1+2 y_2=4 y_1-4 y-4 y_1 \text{ or } y_4+4 y=0 \\
& \Rightarrow k=4
\end{aligned}\)

questions.q: The value of \(\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{\left(4^x-1\right)^3}{\sin \frac{x^2}{4} \log (1+3 x)}\), is
questions.solution:
\(\begin{aligned}
& \lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{\left(4^x-1\right)^3}{\sin \frac{x^2}{4} \log (1+3 x)} \\
& =\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{\left(4^x-1\right)^3}{x^3} \cdot \frac{(x / 2)^2}{\sin x^2 / 4} \cdot \frac{3 x}{\log (1+3 x)} \cdot \frac{4}{3} \\
& =\frac{4}{3}\left(\log _e 4\right)^3 \cdot 1 \cdot \log _e(e)=\frac{4}{3}\left(\log _e 4\right)^3 .
\end{aligned}\)
